subject: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Ross <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker

Morning team + Kevin,

Attaching the March KPI snapshot and a terse QBR deck outline. Highlights:
- 95th p90 latency has drifted ~12% month-over-month on hosted-api for seq len >1024.
- Cost per 1k tokens increased 8% due to higher tail occupancy + fewer cache hits.
- Uptime remains within SLA but we saw two short region blips last week (both recovered).

Primary asks:
1) Marcus — can you validate whether the new batching heuristic rolled on 3/04 caused the latency tail?
2) Tessa — please add a short slide on routing fallback behavior and potential mitigations.
3) Laura — I need a one-paragraph exec note summarizing risk and ETA for fixes.

Kevin — including you here since Atlas will be in the QBR and asked for a short readout on impact to their burst traffic last week. Happy to sync offline if helpful.

Attachments: 2027-03-kpi-snapshot.xlsx, qbr-deck-outline.md

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Kevin Ross <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker

On 2027-03-20 08:12, Soojin Lee wrote:
> Primary asks:
> 1) Marcus — can you validate whether the new batching heuristic rolled on 3/04 caused the latency tail?

Quick update: I ran correlation against rollout windows and found a modest correlation (r~0.4) between the heuristic and increased p90 for long sequences. Preliminary root cause: the heuristic reduces prefix batching for mixed-length requests which increased context cache misses for long tails.

Planned next steps (ETA EOD Tue):
- Re-run the heuristic in staging with KV cache warming enabled.
- Produce a short test harness that simulates Atlas burst pattern (shared in Drive).

I can own the test and a short remediation plan.

-Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kevin Ross <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker

Thanks — adding routing/backoff slides to the outline. A couple of notes for the deck:
- Slide "Mitigations": short-term: enable per-customer prefix caching for Atlas and a conservative batching fallback (no heuristic) for sequences >512.
- Mid-term: automated detection that switches to an efficient KV-warmed path under burst patterns.

I'll attach a one-slide visual of the decision tree. Tentative: put the mitigation summary on slide 4 so execs see it early.

Attachment: latency-breakdown-03-20.pdf (one-slide visual)

-Tessa
Head of Inference Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Ross <kevin@atlasdata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker

Appreciate the heads up, Soojin. Atlas noticed the latency spikes during our nightly ingestion window on 3/16 — that impacted a small set of customers with long sequences.

Questions:
- Can Redwood enable per-tenant prefix cache for Atlas before the QBR?
- If not, what is the expected timeline for the heuristic rollback or safe fallback?

Happy to share our traffic sample if it helps the repro.

Thanks,
Kevin Ross
VP, Platform Engineering
Atlas Data

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Ross <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker

Draft exec blurb below — feel free to refine.

"QBR readout: In March we observed a rise in tail latency for long sequences driven by a new batching heuristic. Impact was isolated and customer-visible for high-burst workloads. Immediate actions include targeted per-tenant cache configuration for affected accounts, temporary conservative batching for long sequences, and a staged rollout of a KV-warm path to eliminate cache-miss-induced spikes. Engineering estimates mitigations in 5 business days for short-term configs and 3–4 sprints for the staged runtime change."

I'll add this to the QBR deck (slide 2) and flag the mitigation ETA.

-Laura
VP, Product — Redwood Console

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Ops leadership KPI sync — QBR prep and action tracker

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Consolidated action items:
- Marcus: run staging validation and share test harness + pulse by 2027-03-22 EOD.
- Tessa: add mitigation slide + include conservative fallback config snippet.
- Laura: finalize exec blurb and drop into Drive QBR folder.
- Dylan: please schedule a 30-min dry run with Atlas next Mon (3/22) to walk the deck and confirm their sample data is captured.

Kevin — we can enable per-tenant prefix cache as a short-term config toggle; I'll loop in infra and get you a timeline by tomorrow morning. Appreciate the Atlas sample — Marcus use that for the harness.

I'll update the thread with the Drive link and final deck once done.

Soojin
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference
